bias_targets.methodology: Conceptual analysis and literature review highlighting stereotype propagation during automated translation from gender-neutral to gender-inflected languages (e.g., defaulting to male for doctors and female for nurses).

Literature review of cultural misalignment in LLM outputs, illustrated by prompting models for localized concepts (e.g., Urdu breakfast foods) and analyzing the generation of Western-centric responses (e.g., bacon and eggs).

Literature review of cross-lingual interference, specifically discussing studies that evaluate how grammatical structures from high-resource languages bleed into translations of low-resource and minority languages.
